title: Basin-lake mass-breeder osmoregulation and buoyancy balance
scope: Foundational freshwater–marine acclimation, passive buoyancy, and longitudinal-balance strategy for the established migratory form governed by WLD-ECOLOGY-006 and WLD-ECOLOGY-007. Exact quantitative physiology, egg and juvenile mechanisms, taxonomy, progression, and human knowledge remain open.
approval_evidence: After 'Salt organs + balance comb' was recommended with separate finite ion-exchange organs, longitudinal wax-like-gel chambers, greater passive support behind the head shield, ordinary biological costs and failures, and strict Mana limits, the Author replied 'yes' on 2026-08-14.
question: What coupled but anatomically separated osmoregulatory and passive-buoyancy strategy should govern the mass breeder's established migratory form?
selection: Use SALT-ORGANS-AND-BALANCE-COMB. Dedicated ion-exchange organs regulate body water and dissolved ions during freshwater–marine acclimation through finite carrier-mediated transport. Separately, multiple small compliant chambers distributed longitudinally contain a metabolically produced low-density wax-like gel, with greater passive buoyant support behind the anterior mineralised shield. The gel contributes passive buoyancy and fore–aft balance without perfect neutral buoyancy, instant adjustment, or depth immunity. Both systems require finite materials, oxygen, energy, time, maintenance, waste handling, recovery, and repair and can lag, saturate, leak, rupture, become infected, or lose effectiveness. Existing ordinary Mana support may reinforce living tissues but cannot create gel mass, move ions without carriers and energy, provide instant acclimation, or act as an activated buoyancy ability.
alternatives: SALT-ORGANS-AND-BALANCE-COMB: separate carrier-based ion-exchange organs and longitudinal wax-like-gel chambers with greater passive buoyant support behind the head shield; selected.
LIVING-SHIELD-ION-BANK: use reversible head-shield mineral loading as an ion buffer and changing anterior ballast; not selected.
SEGMENTED-GAS-LATTICE: use multiple gas chambers linked to respiratory and ion-exchange physiology for lift and trim; not selected.
rationale: The selected package directly addresses salinity transition and the anterior shield's mass while keeping water-and-ion regulation separate from buoyancy material. Distributed non-gas chambers give the alien body a plausible passive support system with ordinary material, metabolic, maintenance, and damage costs, without making one organ solve every problem or granting a cost-free magical ability.
evidence: Author selection on 2026-08-14: after the recommended 'Salt organs + balance comb' package was presented, the Author replied 'yes'.
consequences: The selected systems govern the established migratory form only; egg, juvenile, and other life-stage strategies remain open.
Balance comb is an editorial label for the longitudinal arrangement of internal chambers, not an established in-world term or a comb-shaped organ.
Ion-exchange organs use finite carrier-mediated transport and are distinct from both the respiratory folds and the buoyancy chambers.
Freshwater–marine acclimation consumes time, metabolic energy, and material resources and can lag, saturate, or fail; no salinity immunity or instant switching follows.
Multiple small compliant chambers contain metabolically produced low-density wax-like gel and provide greater passive buoyant support behind the anterior shield.
Passive support contributes to buoyancy and longitudinal trim but does not guarantee neutral buoyancy, effortless hovering, equal performance across salinities or depths, route passage, or survival.
Diet-derived matter, oxygen, energy, internal transport, waste handling, maintenance, recovery, repair, disease, leakage, rupture, and declining condition remain causal constraints.

Mana may reinforce living tissues only; it does not create gel mass, transport ions without carriers and energy, provide instant acclimation, or establish an activated ability, Skill, class, buff, reward, spawn, refill, or free energy.

WLD-ECOLOGY-006 continues to govern migration, egg deposition, adult return and mortality, predation, recruitment, and population variability; WLD-ECOLOGY-007 continues to govern the foundational body plan.
residual_unknowns: Exact salt-organ number, position, exchange surfaces, microanatomy, ion species, carriers, sensors, control loops, waste routes, capacity, thresholds, rates, acclimation duration, and failure thresholds remain open.
Exact gel chemistry, density, compressibility, phase behaviour, synthesis, transport, replenishment, temperature response, and possible metabolic use remain open.
Exact chamber count, position, geometry, connectivity, volume, growth, maintenance, repair, leakage, rupture, infection, and failure thresholds remain open.
Quantitative buoyancy, trim, depth and salinity envelope, shield mass, body size, reproductive and stomach loads, fin contribution, speed, endurance, route energetics, and survival rates remain open.
Egg and juvenile physiology and all developmental differences remain open.
Mana source, carrier, circulation, tissue targets, capacity, cost, recovery, and failure remain open; no new Mana organ or ability is selected.
Taxonomy, species variation, cognition, progression, appraisal, human knowledge, harvesting, material use, and the family-care migrant remain open.
reopening_conditions: Quantitative salinity, buoyancy, trim, temperature, pressure, route, or energy modelling cannot support the selected systems.
Later accepted ecology or story canon creates a concrete contradiction.
The Author explicitly requests a different foundational acclimation or buoyancy strategy.
